headline: Flash flood in Nepal: Many dead and over 1300 missing
seo_title: Flash floods in Nepal: Many dead and over 1300 missing | NZZ

original_de.headline: Sturzflut in Nepal: Viele Tote und über 1300 Vermisste

body.text: **The most important news of the evening:** The flood disaster in Nepal and the death of Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic

**And you'll only read this in the NZZ:** Thousands of citizens were arrested for political reasons during the GDR dictatorship, hundreds murdered. Renate Werwigk-Schneider was imprisoned for weeks in the Stasi prison in Hohenschönhausen in 1963, completely alone, in absolute silence. Even today, she cannot bear the sound of locks snapping shut. Background information

**What happened:** At least 359 people died in the devastating flash flood in the border region between Nepal and China. More than 1,300 remain missing. One Swiss national was rescued. Chinese authorities fear further floods. Chinese state television, citing the Ministry of Water Resources, reported that a dammed lake formed at a river mouth on the Nepalese side. Sources said there was a risk of a dam breach. For the latest developments

**The background:** The flash flood was possibly triggered by a glacier collapse. The fall of ice masses from a great height could have transformed them into water. However, a glacial lake outburst is also possible. In the Himalayas, there are several glacial lakes that must be closely monitored because they can easily breach. The flash flood buried entire settlements over a distance of more than 60 kilometers. For many residents, there was no escape. For background

**The Gyirong border crossing:** The flash flood also destroyed an important border crossing between China and Nepal. It is Beijing's strategic corridor through the Himalayas. A flash flood destroyed the bridge in 2025. Why do Nepal and China nevertheless continue to rely on this dangerous trade route? To the background

**What happened:** Former Bosnian Serb military leader Ratko Mladic died at age 84 in The Hague. Mladic was sentenced to life imprisonment for war crimes and served his sentence in the international prison in The Hague. For the report

**A look back:** Mladic had, among other things, ordered the massacre of more than 8,000 people – mainly men and young men – in the eastern Bosnian enclave of Srebrenica in July 1995. In 2017, he was convicted by the Hague War Crimes Tribunal.

**Yemen in distress: **The radical Houthi tribal militia has been killing fighters of the internationally recognized Yemeni government for weeks. The port city of Aden looks dilapidated after years of wars and crises: only ruins remain of the former luxury hotels, and the plaster peels off the whitewashed facades of the houses. The government wants to retake its country. However, the impending armed conflict in Aden does not meet with great enthusiasm, as a visit shows. For the reportage
With the premium newsletter «NZZ Pro,» you get a look ahead at the global economy and geopolitics. Test it free for 30 days now. Register here

**War remembrance: **The Umbrail is Switzerland's highest drivable pass. Val Müstair celebrated its 125th anniversary this summer. The pass road had its most formative period from 1914 to 1918, when Switzerland defended its neutrality in the war. The ruins of troop camps still stand on the peaks and ridges. A hike with a man who maintains the military historical heritage. For the reportage

**Meta trial:** Arturo Béjar is one of the key figures in the wave of lawsuits against the Instagram company Meta. At Facebook, he led the team that dealt with anti-bullying tools and the protection of minors, among other things. He says: «Instagram is a service that invites strangers into our children's bedrooms, at night.» To the interview

**Smart Glasses: **Anyone filming someone generally needs their consent. Even those filmed by chance must be able to recognize that recording is taking place. Smart glasses undermine this. They make it almost impossible to enforce the right to one's own image. Switzerland is not prepared for this. For the commentary

**🎧 Listen:** Gerald Knaus is one of the most renowned migration researchers in the German-speaking world. He advocates for outsourcing asylum procedures to «safe third countries.» In «NZZ Machtspiel,» the Austrian explains what effects this would have on irregular migration. For the podcast

**📱 Experience:** Digital communication technologies have revolutionized the way we interact. What used to be formal and slow is now casual and fast. But who controls the networks and content? And what does it mean to put an iPad in the hands of toddlers? Discuss at the NZZ Podium on Sept. 3 – on-site or online. Register here
We wish you a pleasant evening.
